text:
Daily Faceoff wrote this week about how Jonathan Lekkerimäki is "realizing his potential with Canucks," and the 22-year-old has made the case easy: 15 points in 21 games after three in 13 last season, with his ice time up more than two minutes a night over his last ten. He scored on the power play against Philadelphia ("a perfectly placed shot," per Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis) and got a look beside Elias Pettersson and Brock Boeser, per The Hockey News' lineup notes.

Some of it is the shot running hot. Seven goals on 4.2 expected goals (the quality of his chances) is 18.9% shooting, above our range for him, and that rarely holds. The context still favors him: of 100 forwards picked 10th to 20th since 2005 with four-plus seasons, the median first full season was 0.35 points a game, and he's at 0.71. His goals have swung games, too (48th of 528 skaters in our wins added). The caveat is five-on-five, where Vancouver has only 40% of the expected goals with him on, about level with its rate without him. He isn't a burner (top speed in the 10th percentile); the release is the weapon.
headline: Jonathan Lekkerimäki's breakthrough, with a shooting asterisk
